subject: anatomy
title: Primitive Gut Tube Subdivisions and Midgut Rotation

steps.tx: Following cephalocaudal and lateral embryonic folding during the fourth week, the endoderm-lined yolk sac cavity is incorporated into the embryo to form the primitive gut tube. The primitive gut is divided into three distinct anatomical territories: the foregut, midgut, and hindgut, each supplied by an independent unpaired **ventral branch of aorta**.
steps.say: Following embryonic folding in the fourth week, part of the yolk sac is incorporated to create the primitive gut tube. The tube divides into three segments: foregut, midgut, and hindgut, each supplied by an unpaired branch from the abdominal aorta.

vis.alt: Foregut, midgut, hindgut divisions and 270 degree rotation sequence
vis.caption: Embryonic gut tube divisions and physiological midgut rotation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The **foregut** extends from the pharyngeal membrane down to the duodenum immediately proximal to the entry of the bile duct at the major duodenal papilla. Supplied by the coeliac trunk, the foregut develops into the esophagus, stomach, first and upper second part of duodenum, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas.
steps.say: The foregut extends from the pharyngeal membrane to the mid-duodenum where the bile duct enters. Perfused by the coeliac trunk, the foregut forms the esophagus, stomach, proximal duodenum, liver, gallbladder, and the pancreas.

rows: Pharyngeal membrane to ampulla of Vater
Ampulla of Vater to left colic flexure
Distal transverse colon to cloacal membrane

steps.tx: The **midgut** begins at the major duodenal papilla and terminates at the junction of the proximal two-thirds and distal third of the transverse colon. Supplied entirely by the superior mesenteric artery, it differentiates into the lower half of the duodenum, jejunum, ileum, cecum, appendix, ascending colon, and proximal transverse colon.
steps.say: The midgut stretches from the major duodenal papilla to the distal third of the transverse colon. Supplied by the superior mesenteric artery, it yields the lower duodenum, small intestine, cecum, appendix, and ascending colon.

points: Origin: Ampulla of Vater in duodenum

right.title: Hindgut Boundaries
points: Origin: Distal third of transverse colon

steps.tx: The hindgut extends from the distal third of the transverse colon to the pectinate line of the anal canal, supplied by the **inferior mesenteric artery**. It forms the distal transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, rectum, and the upper half of the anal canal down to the anal valves.
steps.say: The hindgut spans from the distal transverse colon to the pectinate line of the anal canal, supplied by the inferior mesenteric artery. It forms the left colon, sigmoid, rectum, and upper anal canal mucosa.

steps.tx: During the sixth week, rapid elongation of the midgut loop causes it to outgrow the abdominal cavity. The primary intestinal loop herniates into the extraembryonic coelom of the umbilical cord in a process designated **physiological umbilical herniation**. The loop possesses a cranial duodenojejunal limb and a caudal cecocolic limb, suspended by the superior mesenteric artery axis.
steps.say: In the sixth week, rapid small bowel growth outstrips the abdominal cavity. The midgut loop herniates through the umbilicus into the umbilical cord as a physiological umbilical hernia, rotating around the axis of the superior mesenteric artery.

nodes.label: Total 270 Degree Rotation and Zygosis Fixation

steps.tx: During its stay in the umbilical cord, the midgut loop undergoes an initial ninety-degree counterclockwise rotation around the superior mesenteric artery axis. In the tenth week, the abdomen expands, allowing the herniated loop to return to the peritoneal cavity. During this reduction, the midgut rotates another one hundred and eighty degrees counterclockwise, completing a total **270 degrees counterclockwise rotation**.
steps.say: While in the umbilical cord, the midgut undergoes an initial ninety-degree counterclockwise rotation. In week ten, the bowel returns to the abdomen while rotating another one hundred and eighty degrees, completing a total two hundred and seventy degrees counterclockwise turn.

left.title: Cranial Limb Kinematics
points: Forms the jejunum and proximal ileum
Returns first to the abdomen on week 10
Settles into the left upper quadrant
Pushes hindgut segments to the left flank

right.title: Caudal Limb Kinematics
points: Forms the cecum, appendix, and colon
Cecal bud lands beneath the right liver lobe
Descends into right iliac fossa, forming ascending colon

steps.tx: Upon returning, the jejunal loops enter first and settle into the left upper quadrant. The cecal bud enters last, temporarily lodging in the right upper quadrant beneath the liver before descending into the right iliac fossa. This caudal descent elongates the **ascending colon** and establishes the normal anatomical layout of the large bowel.
steps.say: Upon reduction, jejunal coils enter first to occupy the left upper quadrant. The cecal bud enters last, sitting under the right liver lobe before descending into the right iliac fossa, creating the ascending colon and placing the appendix in the lower right abdomen.

nodes.label: Caudal Descent into Right Iliac Fossa

steps.tx: Arrest of midgut rotation can cause intestinal malrotation, wherein the small intestine remains entirely on the right and the colon on the left. Peritoneal bands called **Ladd bands** cross the duodenum to anchor the misplaced cecum, causing acute extrinsic duodenal obstruction and predisposing to midgut volvulus around the narrow superior mesenteric vascular stalk.
steps.say: Arrested midgut rotation causes intestinal malrotation, leaving the small bowel on the right and the colon on the left. Fibrous Ladd bands cross the duodenum to tether the misplaced cecum, causing extrinsic duodenal obstruction and predisposing to twisting midgut volvulus.

rows: Small intestine on right, colon on left
